title: Site and bond percolation thresholds of all $k$-uniform tilings with $k\le 10$
abstract: We determine the site and bond percolation thresholds of all 23,396 $k$-uniform tilings of the plane by regular polygons with $k\le 10$, the complete set according to the known enumeration. We use Monte Carlo simulation on tori and the condition that no wrapping and a cross-wrapping cluster are equally probable, the Monte Carlo form of the critical-polynomial criterion, which needs no knowledge of the large-scale anisotropy that most of these lattices have. The 486 thresholds with $k\le4$ have uncertainties of a few units in the sixth decimal and reproduce the 22 Archimedean reference values (rms deviation 0.71 standard errors) and unpublished bond thresholds of the 20 two-uniform lattices ($χ^2=19.5$ for 20 values); the others have median statistical uncertainties of $2\times10^{-5}$ ($k\le7$) to $7\times10^{-5}$ ($k\ge8$) and no detectable finite-size bias. The vertex-type fractions alone fix the thresholds for $k\ge5$ to about $2\times10^{-3}$ (linear rule fitted on $k\le4$), while tilings with equal composition differ by up to $6\times10^{-3}$ (site) and $2\times10^{-2}$ (bond). In the range of domain sizes covered, descriptors of radius one account for more than half of this difference, and stackings of identical strips have thresholds linear in the fraction of each boundary type. For tilings that differ only by the registry of strips separated by $h$ rows of squares, the bond threshold difference decreases by a factor of 6-8 per row, comparable to the leading momentum-$π$ eigenvalue of the square-band transfer matrix.
summary: This work calculates the site and bond percolation thresholds for a vast set of 23,396 regular polygon tilings. Using advanced Monte Carlo simulations on tori, the authors establish precise critical probabilities, confirming consistency with known lattice results and providing new data for complex quasi-periodic structures.
main_problem: The paper aims to determine the site and bond percolation thresholds for all 23,396 k-uniform tilings of the plane for k up to 10.
main_result: The authors provide calculated thresholds for these tilings, showing high precision for k<=4 and demonstrating how vertex-type fractions predict thresholds for higher k.
method: The primary method involves Monte Carlo simulations on tori using the critical-polynomial criterion, which compares the probabilities of no wrapping versus cross-wrapping clusters.
model_or_system: The system under study is the plane tiled by regular polygons, specifically focusing on k-uniform tilings. These tilings are analyzed using percolation theory concepts.
key_observables: Site and bond percolation thresholds (p_c), probabilities of cluster wrapping (P_0(p) and P_+(p)).
important_parameters: The number of polygons k (up to 10), the size of the torus (N_s), and the percolation probability p.
main_assumptions: The critical criterion relies on the equality of probabilities of no wrapping and cross-wrapping cluster, and the analysis assumes the critical model on a torus approaches isotropic critical percolation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate examples of k-uniform tilings (k=3, 9, 10) and compare calculated thresholds against known Archimedean reference values.
paper_structure: The paper details the methodology using Monte Carlo simulations on tori, presents the results for k<=4 reproducing known values, and discusses the extrapolation and analysis for k>=5 based on vertex-type fractions.
why_interesting: While focused on classical percolation, the rigorous statistical mechanics techniques (Monte Carlo, critical exponents, transfer matrices) are foundational to understanding phase transitions in quantum many-body systems.
